display.title: Episode 349: The Flickering Flame and I Love Hashem
display.summary_short: A shoemaker's lamp teaches Rabbi Yisrael of Salant that as long as the candle burns we can still repair, and a boy shows his mother what a mirror teaches about simcha.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the week of Parshas Vayeira 5749. Uncle Yossi reminds listeners to send in letters about turning their homes into a mitzvah with a tzedakah pushka, for a chance at a gift certificate. After the Hakochainik march, a first-grade class from a Boro Park girls' school leads the Shema, followed by the sponsor. Story time begins with the Baal Shem Tov's teaching that we can learn a lesson from everything we see and hear. Rabbi Yisrael of Salant, out late at night collecting tzedakah for the poor, finds a shoemaker still at work by lamplight. The shoemaker explains that he always works as long as his lamp burns, and tonight he poured in too much oil. Rabbi Yisrael is overjoyed by the lesson: as long as the candle of the soul burns, we can still repair and do teshuvah. In a second story, little Beryl borrows his mother's mirror to show what his Rebbe taught: a happy face is reflected back with happiness, so we should serve Hashem with simcha, for we are Jewish, we have the Torah and mitzvos, and each one brings us closer to Hashem. Beryl sings 'I Love Hashem', and the show ends with Shabbos candle time.
display.lesson: As long as we are alive we can still improve and do teshuvah, and if we serve Hashem with a happy face, Hashem shines happiness back to us.

date.note: Consistent with the audio: Shabbos candles on Friday 4 November.
